title: The category of families of objects has finite limits
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category with a final object $e$ and fibre products (for instance the small etale site $X_{\Et}$ of a scheme $X$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], with final object $\mathrm{id}_X$). Let $\mathrm{FC}(\mathcal C)$ be the category whose objects are families $\{U_i\}_{i\in I}$ of objects of $\mathcal C$ indexed by sets, whose morphisms $\{U_i\}_{i\in I}\to\{V_j\}_{j\in J}$ are pairs $(\alpha,(f_i)_{i\in I})$ of a map $\alpha:I\to J$ and morphisms $f_i:U_i\to V_{\alpha(i)}$ of $\mathcal C$, and whose composition is $(\beta,(g_j))\circ(\alpha,(f_i))=(\beta\circ\alpha,(g_{\alpha(i)}\circ f_i))$. Then: (1) the one-member family $\{e\}$ is a final object of $\mathrm{FC}(\mathcal C)$; (2) for morphisms $(\alpha,f_i):\{U_i\}_{i\in I}\to\{V_j\}_{j\in J}$ and $(\beta,g_k):\{W_k\}_{k\in K}\to\{V_j\}_{j\in J}$, the family $\{U_i\times_{f_i,V_{\alpha(i)},g_k}W_k\}_{(i,k)\in I\times K,\ \alpha(i)=\beta(k)}$ with its two projections is a fibre product in $\mathrm{FC}(\mathcal C)$; (3) consequently $\mathrm{FC}(\mathcal C)$ has all finite limits.
